summary: I changed one file, `solution/core.py`, and the visible suite now passes (2 passed). The bug was in the merge step of `merge`: when an interval overlapped the previous one, the code replaced the merged result with `(pa, b)`, taking the new interval's end instead of whichever end was larger. That made sense only when the new interval reached further. When it sat inside the previous one, as with `(1, 4)` and `(2, 3)`, or `(1, 3)` and the point `(2, 2)`, the merged result got shorter and became `(1, 3)` or `(1, 2)`. The fix keeps the larger end with `out[-1] = (pa, max(pb, b))`, so it applies to every overlap rather than to the tested inputs only. I also checked a few other cases by hand: touching intervals still join when `join_touching` is on and stay separate when it's off, an interval holding one and overlapping another merges to `(1, 6)`, and duplicate points collapse to one. One thing I left as it was: with `join_touching=False`, a point sitting exactly on the previous interval's end, like `(1, 2)` and `(2, 2)`, is still kept separate. The original condition seems to do that on purpose, and the issue doesn't say otherwise.
